findings.text: after_suite.command records `pytest -m graph --durations=0 ...` but logs/gate-head.log's own header line records `pytest -m graph -s --durations=0 ...`; the recorded command, re-run, would capture the fixture's receipt line instead of printing it, so the one log line the fragment cites as the post-session check would not appear.

the OSError fallback to a rename failure calls directory.cleanup(), which performs the same unbounded recursive delete inside the session's teardown that the node exists to take off that path; the failure is reported only after it has blocked, so on a filesystem where the rename fails the budget the node claims is not held.

the store removal runs in a finally around temp_neo4j.stop_temp_neo4j, so when the stop itself raises (it can, after its SIGKILL timeout) a removal failure raised from the finally replaces the stop's exception; the teardown still fails, but the traceback named is the removal's and the stop failure is lost.
